name: Plate food attractively
blurb: Presentation is a small set of learnable rules about height, negative space, colour and sauce placement. The same food looks twice as good with ten minutes of thought.
gear: A squeeze bottle and a small offset spatula
Tweezers if you are feeling serious
steps: Start with the plate: plain, larger than you need, and warmed for hot food.
Build height at the centre rather than spreading everything flat — one focal point, not four competing ones.
Leave negative space. Crowding is the most common home-cook fault.
Place sauce deliberately: a pool underneath, a swipe, or dots — never poured over the top where it hides everything.
Add colour and texture contrast: something green, something crisp, something acidic.
Wipe the rim clean before serving and photograph your plates to review them honestly.
tips: Odd numbers look better than even ones. Three scallops, not four.
Garnish must be edible and relevant. Decorative herbs nobody eats look dated.
proof: You plate a normal weeknight meal so it would not look out of place in a restaurant photo.
